prompt: The pitch boasts 1 million downloads, but only 3% opened the app twice.
why: Downloads look big but don't show value. Vanity metric.
trap: Retention is the real story; the clue is the hollow number.

prompt: Pageviews doubled after splitting articles into ten pages each.
tells: after splitting articles into ten pages
why: Inflating a number without more value is a vanity metric.
trap: It went up, but nothing improved.

prompt: The chart of total sign-ups ever can only go up.
why: Cumulative totals hide declines. Vanity metric.
trap: It isn't wrong data; it's an uninformative view.

prompt: The team celebrates 50,000 followers, but none of it led to a single sale.
tells: none of it led to a single sale
why: Numbers disconnected from outcomes are vanity.
trap: It's not about segmenting; the metric is hollow.

prompt: Asked what they'd do differently if the number dropped, nobody had an answer.
why: A metric that doesn't change decisions is vanity.
trap: The test of a metric is whether it drives action.

prompt: 'Registered users' counts accounts that never finished onboarding.
why: Counting empty accounts flatters the product.
trap: Segmenting would expose it; the number itself is vanity.
